changed.title: For k ≥ 8 the one-round shared-key test on two k-bit names uses at most 36k·2^⌊k/2⌋ fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates
changed.statement:
∀ k : Nat, 8 ≤ k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    let x := rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName
    step (x ^^^ rot 1 x ^^^ rot (k - 1) x) ^^^ rot 0 rowKey ^^^ constant 1
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    let z := rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName
    step (z ^^^ rot 2 z ^^^ rot (k - 2) z) ^^^ rot 4 colKey ^^^ constant 2
  let slots := 2 ^ (k - (k + 1) / 2)
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < slots) && decide (second w col.val < slots))
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ slots * (36 * k) ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits
changed.unlocks: a circuit ceiling for adjacency after one round of the shared-key rule at every width of at least eight
changed.context: On paper. Set h=ceil(k/2), S=2^(k-h), x=rot1(w) XOR u. For each setting of the four seed bits and k-h-4 free bits, solve the h row equations in descending order. Bit i fixes x[i-1] from x[i..i+3] in at most 23 gates. Every passing key belongs to exactly its seed and free bits. Recover w, evaluate the column test in that slot, AND its h pass wires, then OR all slots. Four gates implement XOR. Counting the shared constants and output tree gives S(35h+16k)+2 <= 36kS. Append gates in order.

changed.title: A cyclic window determines how changing the far starting bit affects a row-test output
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat) (u : Fin (2 ^ k)) (c : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k)),
  1 ≤ r → r ≠ 3 →
  let left := max r (2 * r - 3)
  let width := left + 3 * r
  width < k →
  let rot := fun (s w : Nat) =>
    ((w <<< (s % k)) ||| (w >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (x : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (x.testBit i)
        (!(x.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && x.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let start := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) => rot 1 w.val ^^^ u.val
  let state := fun (w : Fin (2 ^ k)) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun prev j =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * j) w.val ^^^ (c (j + 1)).val)
      (start w)
  ∀ (i : Fin k) (w v : Fin (2 ^ k)),
    let p := (i.val + k - left) % k
    (∀ j : Fin width,
      (start w).testBit ((p + 1 + j.val) % k) =
      (start v).testBit ((p + 1 + j.val) % k)) →
    xor ((state w).testBit i.val) ((state v).testBit i.val) =
      xor ((start w).testBit p) ((start v).testBit p)
changed.unlocks: supplies the actual row-test pivot needed to recover starting bits in the cyclic slot bijection before the window wraps
changed.context: On paper. Write x for the rotated key XOR the row. In round t the state path reads offsets -1 through +3 of the previous state. The re-added key contributes x at offset 3-2t. At one round the linear left endpoint is -1. At two only the previous bit at -1 carries endpoint -2. Induction bounds the state support by [-max(t,2t-3),3t]. From round four the final key bit lies strictly left of the entire state path. The width hypothesis prevents aliasing. The fixed neighboring bits cancel when the two outputs are XORed.

From round four the final key bit lies strictly left of the entire state path. The width hypothesis prevents aliasing. The fixed neighboring bits cancel when the two outputs are XORed.

changed.title: For r ≥ 3 and k ≥ 7r - 1, at most 2^max(floor(k/2),7r - 2) keys pass the second test at any fixed k-bit column
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 3 ≤ r → 7 * r - 1 ≤ k → ∀ v : Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  ((List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun w => decide (second w v.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))).length
    ≤ 2 ^ (max (k - h) (7 * r - 2))
changed.unlocks: Bounds the number of keys a column can admit from three rounds onward, for the column-side circuit construction.
changed.context: On paper. Fix v and write z = rot3(w) XOR v, a bijection. Each round reads previous offsets -2 through 4 and adds z at offset 2-3t. Inductively the left reach after t rounds is at most max(2t,3t-2), the right reach 4t. At r >= 3 the last key supplies z[p] at p=i-(3r-2), before a window z[p+1..p+L] with L=7r-2. Sweep down the h tested bits. The initial q=min(h,k-L) pivots are fresh. Equal bits off these pivots force equal pivot bits in order for passing words. Later cyclic checks can only discard assignments. Count the 2^(k-q) choices off the pivots.
